text:
I see you are a newborn; please tell me if you were born prematurely and if your birth was complicated by any issues like fetal distress or difficult delivery. Additionally, have you noticed any specific symptoms such as blue discoloration of your skin or a rapid breathing rate since birth?

REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas, Complete_Blood_Count, Blood_Culture

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The clinical presentation of grunting, retractions, and peripheral cyanosis in a newborn is classic for RDS, likely due to surfactant deficiency; the previous suggestion of tuberculosis is incorrect and unrelated to this acute respiratory failure pattern. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.
